title: Deepika and Ranveer Name Second Daughter Devi in a Dussehra Reveal
excerpt: Born on September 19, Devi Padukone Singh was introduced in the family's first portrait of four, her name, meaning goddess, paired with elder sister Dua, meaning prayer.
body:
• Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh used Dussehra to announce their second daughter's name: Devi Padukone Singh, in a joint social media post captioned "Of Love & Abundance."
  • Devi was born on September 19. Her elder sister Dua, born in September 2024, appears in the family's first portrait of four, kissing her baby sister.
  • Devi, from Sanskrit, means goddess. It pairs deliberately with Dua, which means prayer.
  • The couple, married at Lake Como in November 2018, have shared their children's milestones sparingly: a footprint at birth, a name weeks later.

Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh have named their second daughter Devi Padukone Singh, revealing the name on Dussehra in a joint social media post with the family's first portrait of four.

"Of Love & Abundance... Devi Padukone Singh," the couple captioned the photograph, according to Bollywood Hungama. Devi was born on September 19.

A Portrait, Carefully Staged

The photograph shows the family in coordinated ivory and gold ethnic outfits. Deepika holds the newborn while their elder daughter Dua, born on September 8, 2024, leans in to kiss her sister. Ranveer stands alongside, in what Pinkvilla described as a portrait that drew congratulatory comments from Bipasha Basu, Sharvari, Veer Pahariya, Bhumi Pednekar, Sanjay Kapoor and Huma Qureshi, among others. Alia Bhatt, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Karisma Kapoor responded with heart and shine emojis, ANI reported.

https://x.com/MissMalini/status/2112566047098429595

The timing was chosen, not incidental. Dussehra marks the victory of good over evil, and Devi, the divine feminine, is at the centre of the festival season's worship. Announcing a daughter named Devi, meaning goddess, on that day needs no further explanation, and the couple offered none.

Two Names, One Pattern

Dua means prayer. Devi means goddess. Together the names form a small, deliberate pair, traditional in meaning and short in form, and they continue the naming pattern the couple set in November 2024, when they announced Dua's name weeks after her birth with a photograph of her feet.

Devi's arrival followed the same choreography: a birth announcement on September 19 built around a footprint, then the name a month later, on a festival day, with a single portrait. For two of India's most photographed actors, the restraint is the story. The children appear on the parents' terms, at milestones, and not in between.

The Couple Behind the Post

Deepika and Ranveer married on November 14, 2018, at Lake Como in Italy, in ceremonies following both Konkani and Sindhi traditions. Work resumes around the family news: Ranveer was last seen leading Dhurandhar: The Revenge, while Deepika's upcoming slate includes King alongside Shah Rukh Khan.

For diaspora fans, who followed the wedding, Dua's birth and now Devi's naming as shared cultural moments, the announcement landed exactly as designed: a festival greeting, a name with a meaning worth repeating, and one photograph.

What's Next

If the pattern holds, the next family update will come at the next milestone, and not before. Until then, the family of four has a name for its newest member, and it was announced on the one day of the year when that name is on every greeting card in the country.
